name: Semaglutide
tagline: Gold-standard weekly GLP-1 for weight loss & glucose control
description: Semaglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist approved for type 2 diabetes (Ozempic) and chronic weight management (Wegovy). It significantly reduces appetite, slows gastric emptying, and improves glycemic control.
mechanism: Mimics endogenous GLP-1, binding to GLP-1 receptors in the pancreas (stimulating insulin release), hypothalamus (reducing appetite), and gut (slowing gastric emptying).
usage: Subcutaneous injection once weekly. Dose titrated up every 4 weeks to minimise GI side effects. Available as brand-name pens (Ozempic/Wegovy) or compounded vials.

name: Tirzepatide
tagline: Dual GLP-1/GIP agonist with superior weight-loss results
description: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro / Zepbound) is the first dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 receptor agonist. Clinical trials show up to 22% body-weight reduction, surpassing semaglutide.
mechanism: Activates both GIP and GLP-1 receptors simultaneously, producing additive effects on insulin secretion, appetite suppression, and fat oxidation.
usage: Once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Dose escalation from 2.5 mg every 4 weeks up to 15 mg maximum.

name: Liraglutide
tagline: Once-daily GLP-1 with proven cardiovascular benefits
description: Liraglutide (Victoza/Saxenda) is a daily GLP-1 receptor agonist. At 1.2–1.8 mg doses it treats T2D; at 3 mg it is approved for chronic weight management. It was the first GLP-1 to demonstrate CV risk reduction in the LEADER trial.
mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonism leading to glucose-dependent insulin secretion, glucagon suppression, and appetite reduction via central hypothalamic pathways.
usage: Once-daily subcutaneous injection, titrated up over 4 weeks. Inject in abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.

name: BPC-157
tagline: Gut-derived healing peptide with potent regenerative effects
description: Body Protection Compound 157 is a 15-amino-acid peptide derived from human gastric juice. Research shows accelerated healing of tendons, ligaments, muscle, and gut lining. It has no approved human indication but is widely studied in animal models.
mechanism: Upregulates growth hormone receptors, promotes angiogenesis (new blood vessel formation), modulates nitric oxide pathways, and stimulates tendon fibroblast outgrowth.
usage: Subcutaneous or intramuscular injection near the site of injury, or oral/systemic for gut health. Typically cycled 4–8 weeks on, 2–4 weeks off.

name: TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4)
tagline: Systemic tissue repair and anti-inflammatory peptide
description: TB-500 is a synthetic version of Thymosin Beta-4, an actin-sequestering protein found in nearly all human cells. It promotes healing, reduces inflammation, and may improve flexibility and angiogenesis.
mechanism: Regulates actin polymerisation, promotes cell migration and differentiation, inhibits inflammatory cytokines, and upregulates laminin-5 for tissue repair.
usage: Subcutaneous or intramuscular injection, typically 2–2.5 mg twice per week during loading phase, then 1–2 mg weekly for maintenance.

name: CJC-1295
tagline: Long-acting GHRH analogue for sustained GH release
description: CJC-1295 is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). The DAC (Drug Affinity Complex) form binds albumin extending its half-life to days, producing sustained elevation of GH and IGF-1 levels.
mechanism: Binds and activates GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotrophs, stimulating pulsatile growth hormone secretion and downstream IGF-1 production.
usage: Subcutaneous injection once or twice weekly (DAC form). Often stacked with Ipamorelin for synergistic GH pulse amplification.

name: Ipamorelin
tagline: Selective GH secretagogue with minimal side-effect profile
description: Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide ghrelin mimetic and GH secretagogue receptor (GHSR) agonist. It is highly selective — stimulating GH without meaningful cortisol, prolactin, or ACTH elevation, making it one of the cleanest GH peptides.
mechanism: Selectively activates GHSR-1a on pituitary cells, inducing pulsatile GH release without affecting non-target endocrine axes.
usage: Subcutaneous injection 2–3× daily, ideally fasted and away from meals. Commonly stacked with CJC-1295 or Sermorelin.

name: Sermorelin
tagline: Physiological GHRH analogue for restoring youthful GH pulses
description: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of endogenous GHRH. It is FDA-approved for paediatric GH deficiency and widely used off-label for anti-ageing and body composition. It works within the natural feedback loop, unlike exogenous HGH.
mechanism: Binds GHRH receptors on anterior pituitary, stimulating GH synthesis and pulsatile release while preserving natural regulatory feedback.
usage: Subcutaneous injection at bedtime to mimic the natural nocturnal GH surge. Often used daily for 3–6 month cycles.

name: AOD-9604
tagline: Modified HGH fragment targeting fat metabolism
description: AOD-9604 is a modified fragment of human growth hormone (hGH176-191) designed to stimulate lipolysis and inhibit lipogenesis without the insulin resistance or proliferative effects of full hGH.
mechanism: Activates beta-3 adrenergic receptors in adipose tissue, stimulates lipolysis (fat breakdown), inhibits lipogenesis, and may promote cartilage repair via GH-like pathways.
usage: Subcutaneous injection, fasted state preferred. Typically used in cycles targeting fat loss alongside caloric deficit.

name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
tagline: Melanocortin agonist for sexual function and libido
description: PT-141, now FDA-approved as Vyleesi for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women, is a synthetic melanocortin analogue. It acts centrally to increase sexual desire and arousal in both sexes.
mechanism: Agonises MC3R and MC4R melanocortin receptors in the CNS, activating dopaminergic pathways in the hypothalamus associated with sexual motivation.
usage: Subcutaneous injection 45–60 minutes before sexual activity. Not for daily use; typical dosing is as-needed, maximum 1× per 24 hours.

name: MK-677 (Ibutamoren)
tagline: Oral GH secretagogue for muscle, sleep, and recovery
description: MK-677 is a non-peptide, orally active ghrelin mimetic and GH secretagogue. It raises GH and IGF-1 levels without affecting cortisol, making it attractive for lean mass gains, sleep improvement, and recovery.
mechanism: Selectively activates GHSR-1a, mimicking ghrelin to stimulate GH pulses from the pituitary. Oral bioavailability eliminates the need for injections.
usage: Taken orally, typically at bedtime to coincide with natural GH secretion. Cycles of 3–6 months are common; some use year-round at lower doses.

name: IGF-1 LR3
tagline: Extended-action IGF-1 analogue for muscle hypertrophy
description: IGF-1 LR3 is a recombinant IGF-1 analogue with an arginine substitution and N-terminal extension that dramatically extends half-life vs native IGF-1. It promotes muscle cell proliferation, differentiation, and satellite cell activation.
mechanism: Binds IGF-1 receptors with reduced binding to IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), prolonging activity. Activates PI3K/Akt/mTOR and MAPK/ERK pathways driving anabolism.
usage: Subcutaneous or intramuscular injection post-workout. Short cycles (4–6 weeks) recommended due to potential receptor desensitisation.

name: Epithalon
tagline: Telomere-extending tetrapeptide with anti-ageing potential
description: Epithalon (Epitalon) is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) derived from the pineal gland peptide Epithalamin. Research suggests it activates telomerase, extends telomere length, and may slow biological ageing.
mechanism: Activates telomerase enzyme, promotes melatonin production, regulates circadian rhythms, and may modulate p53 tumour suppressor activity.
usage: Subcutaneous or IV injection in courses of 10–20 days. Typically 2× per year. Nasal spray formulations also used.

name: Selank
tagline: Anxiolytic peptide that enhances cognition without sedation
description: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide analogue of tuftsin developed by the Institute of Molecular Genetics (Russia). It is approved in Russia for anxiety disorders and shows nootropic, anti-anxiety, and neuroprotective effects.
mechanism: Modulates expression of BDNF, serotonin, and dopaminergic systems. Stabilises enkephalin degradation and may enhance immune function via IL-6 pathway.
usage: Intranasal spray or subcutaneous injection. Short courses of 10–14 days for anxiety; longer-term for cognition enhancement.

name: Semax
tagline: ACTH-derived nootropic with BDNF-boosting and neuroprotective action
description: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide derived from the ACTH(4-7) sequence. It is clinically used in Russia for stroke, ischemia, and cognitive impairment. Users report improved focus, memory, and stress resilience.
mechanism: Rapidly elevates BDNF and NGF in hippocampus and frontal cortex; modulates serotonin and dopamine reuptake; protects neurons from oxidative stress.
usage: Intranasal administration is most common (nasal spray). Subcutaneous injection also used. Short courses of 10–14 days.

name: Dihexa
tagline: Potent nootropic peptide with synaptogenic effects
description: Dihexa is an N-hexanoic-Tyr-Ile-(6) aminohexanoic amide, derived from angiotensin IV. Animal studies show 7 orders of magnitude more potent cognitive enhancement than BDNF in some models, with pro-social and memory-enhancing properties.
mechanism: Facilitates HGF/c-Met signalling to potentiate NMDA receptor function, promotes synaptogenesis, and enhances dendritic spine density in the hippocampus.
usage: Transdermal cream, sublingual, or oral capsule. Used in very small quantities; typical cycles 2–4 weeks.

name: SS-31 (Elamipretide)
tagline: Mitochondria-targeted peptide for energy and cellular repair
description: SS-31 (Szeto-Schiller peptide 31) selectively concentrates in the inner mitochondrial membrane where it stabilises cardiolipin, improving electron transport chain efficiency. Clinical trials show benefit in heart failure and mitochondrial myopathies.
mechanism: Selectively partitions to inner mitochondrial membrane via electrostatic attraction; stabilises cardiolipin to preserve cristae architecture, reducing ROS and improving ATP synthesis.
usage: Subcutaneous injection. Used in cycles for cellular energy optimisation. Clinical trial doses higher than typical research protocols.

name: MOTS-c
tagline: Mitochondrial-encoded peptide that activates AMPK and metabolism
description: MOTS-c is a 16-amino acid peptide encoded by the mitochondrial genome (12S rRNA gene). It activates AMPK, improves insulin sensitivity, regulates glucose metabolism, and shows exercise-mimicking effects in animal studies.
mechanism: Activates AMPK and SIRT1 pathways, inhibits the folate cycle and de novo purine synthesis (raising ZMP → AMPK), reduces lipid accumulation, and improves skeletal muscle glucose uptake.
usage: Subcutaneous injection. Research protocols commonly use 5–10 mg doses 3–5× per week.

name: Humanin
tagline: Mitochondrial-derived peptide with cytoprotective longevity effects
description: Humanin is a 21-amino acid peptide also encoded within the mitochondrial 16S rRNA gene. It protects neurons from amyloid-beta toxicity, improves insulin sensitivity, and correlates inversely with biological age in humans.
mechanism: Binds the cytokine receptor gp130 and IL-6 receptor, activating JAK2/STAT3 pathways. Directly inhibits pro-apoptotic proteins (Bax, tBid) and reduces inflammatory cytokine signalling.
usage: Subcutaneous injection. Research protocols use 1–2 mg doses several times per week.

name: GHRP-2
tagline: Potent GH secretagogue with appetite stimulation
description: GHRP-2 (Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide 2) is a synthetic hexapeptide that strongly stimulates GH release. It is more potent than GHRP-6 but with less pronounced appetite stimulation, making it popular for body composition protocols.
mechanism: Binds GHSR-1a receptors, potently stimulating GH secretion from the pituitary. Also has mild anti-inflammatory effects via NF-κB pathway modulation.
usage: Subcutaneous injection in fasted state, typically 3× daily. Often combined with a GHRH analogue (CJC-1295 or Sermorelin) for synergistic GH release.

name: GHRP-6
tagline: Classic GH secretagogue with strong appetite-stimulating effects
description: GHRP-6 is a first-generation hexapeptide GH secretagogue. It produces robust GH pulses and is frequently used in research and off-label for GH restoration. The strong appetite increase can be a feature (for bulking) or a drawback.
mechanism: Binds GHSR-1a ghrelin receptors, stimulating pituitary GH release and gastric motility. The ghrelin-like appetite effect is more pronounced than GHRP-2.
usage: Subcutaneous injection, fasted, 30 min before meals or post-workout. Commonly combined with CJC-1295 for a 'GHRH + GHRP' synergistic stack.

name: Hexarelin
tagline: Most potent GHRP with cardioprotective secondary effects
description: Hexarelin is the most potent synthetic GHRP, producing the largest acute GH pulses. It also activates GHS-R1b receptors in the heart, demonstrating cardioprotective and anti-fibrotic properties independent of GH release.
mechanism: Potent GHSR-1a agonist for pituitary GH release. Also binds cardiac GHS-R and CD36 receptor, providing direct cardioprotection and lipid clearance.
usage: Subcutaneous injection in fasted state. Due to rapid GH desensitisation, cycles of 4 weeks on, 4 weeks off are common.

name: Tesamorelin
tagline: FDA-approved GHRH analogue for visceral fat reduction in HIV
description: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is the only FDA-approved GHRH analogue, indicated for lipodystrophy-related visceral fat accumulation in HIV patients. Off-label, it is studied for visceral fat reduction and cognitive function in older adults.
mechanism: Binds GHRH receptors with high affinity, stimulating pulsatile GH release. Downstream IGF-1 elevation reduces visceral adipose tissue and may improve neurocognitive function.
usage: Subcutaneous injection, 2 mg daily in the evening. FDA-approved dosing uses daily injections.

name: PYY (Peptide YY)
tagline: Gut-derived satiety hormone that reduces appetite post-meal
description: Peptide YY (PYY) is a 36-amino acid gut hormone released by L-cells in the distal intestine in response to food. PYY3-36 is the biologically active truncated form and acts centrally to reduce food intake.
mechanism: Binds Y2 receptors in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus, inhibiting NPY/AgRP neurons to reduce hunger signals. Also slows gastric emptying and intestinal motility.
usage: Subcutaneous injection research protocols. Circulates naturally post-meal; exogenous dosing used in obesity research.

name: GIP (Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide)
tagline: Incretin hormone targeted by tirzepatide for enhanced metabolic benefit
description: GIP is one of the two major incretin hormones, released by K-cells in the duodenum and jejunum. Its receptor is the second target of tirzepatide. GIP receptor agonism appears synergistic with GLP-1 agonism for weight loss.
mechanism: Stimulates insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner, enhances bone formation, and may reduce nausea side effects of GLP-1 agonism when combined.
usage: No standalone exogenous GIP products available; targeted by combination agents like tirzepatide.

name: LL-37
tagline: Host-defence peptide with antimicrobial and wound-healing properties
description: LL-37 is the only human member of the cathelicidin family of antimicrobial peptides. It is produced by immune cells, keratinocytes, and epithelial cells. Beyond antimicrobial activity, it promotes wound healing, angiogenesis, and modulates inflammation.
mechanism: Disrupts microbial membranes via amphipathic helix insertion; activates FPR2 and EGFR receptors to stimulate keratinocyte migration and proliferation; promotes angiogenesis via VEGF pathway.
usage: Subcutaneous injection or topical application. Research protocols use 100–500 mcg doses for wound healing or immune modulation.

name: KPV
tagline: Alpha-MSH fragment with potent gut anti-inflammatory action
description: KPV (Lys-Pro-Val) is the C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH). It retains α-MSH's anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. Oral KPV shows promise for inflammatory bowel disease in animal models.
mechanism: Binds melanocortin receptors (MC1R, MC3R) and may act via receptor-independent mechanisms in the colon. Inhibits NF-κB signalling and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6).
usage: Oral capsule or sublingual. Subcutaneous injection also used. Typically cycled 4–8 weeks.

name: Larazotide (AT-1001)
tagline: Tight-junction peptide that reduces intestinal permeability
description: Larazotide acetate is an 8-amino acid peptide that targets zonulin-mediated opening of intestinal tight junctions. It has been studied in coeliac disease and leaky gut conditions, showing reduction in intestinal permeability markers.
mechanism: Directly preserves tight junction integrity by inhibiting zonulin-mediated paracellular permeability. Reduces translocation of antigens and pathogens across the gut epithelium.
usage: Oral capsule, taken with meals. Research doses of 0.25–1 mg three times daily with meals.

name: GHK-Cu (Copper Peptide)
tagline: Copper-binding tripeptide that promotes collagen synthesis and skin repair
description: GHK-Cu is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide (Gly-His-Lys-Cu²⁺) found in human plasma, saliva, and urine. Concentrations decline with age. It promotes collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycan synthesis and has wound-healing, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties.
mechanism: Binds copper ions, delivering them to enzymes involved in connective tissue synthesis. Activates over 4000 genes involved in wound healing, stem cell activation, and skin remodelling.
usage: Topical cream/serum for skin (most common). Subcutaneous injection for systemic use. Research injections often 0.5–2 mg/day.

name: SNAP-8
tagline: Botox-alternative peptide that reduces expression lines topically
description: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3) is a synthetic octapeptide that mimics the N-terminal end of SNAP-25, competing for binding in the SNARE complex. This reduces acetylcholine vesicle release at the neuromuscular junction, decreasing facial muscle contractions.
mechanism: Competes with SNAP-25 for SNARE complex binding, modulating the docking of acetylcholine vesicles and reducing neuromuscular contraction amplitude.
usage: Topical application in face creams at 5–10% concentration. Not typically injected subcutaneously.

name: FOXO4-DRI
tagline: Senolytic peptide that selectively clears senescent cells
description: FOXO4-DRI is a retro-inverso peptide that disrupts the interaction between FOXO4 and p53 inside senescent cells, triggering apoptosis. In mouse studies it reversed physical deterioration and restored fur density, fitness, and renal function.
mechanism: Antagonises the FOXO4-p53 interaction in senescent cells, removing FOXO4-mediated survival signalling and restoring p53-driven apoptosis specifically in senescent (not healthy) cells.
usage: Subcutaneous injection in research protocols. Typically pulsed dosing (3 consecutive days per month) rather than continuous.

name: Thymosin Alpha-1
tagline: Thymic peptide that modulates and enhances immune function
description: Thymosin Alpha-1 (Tα1) is an endogenous 28-amino acid peptide secreted by thymic epithelial cells. FDA-designated Orphan Drug (Zadaxin) with approval in several countries for hepatitis B/C and as an adjuvant in cancer immunotherapy.
mechanism: Activates dendritic cells, T-cell differentiation, and natural killer cells. Modulates TLR signalling and cytokine production (upregulates IL-2, IFN-γ, downregulates IL-4, IL-5).
usage: Subcutaneous injection. Typical protocols: 1.6 mg twice weekly for immune modulation, or daily for acute conditions.

name: Exenatide (Byetta)
tagline: First GLP-1 agonist — twice-daily option for T2D
description: Exenatide was the first GLP-1 receptor agonist approved (2005). Derived from Gila monster salivary protein Exendin-4, it shares ~50% homology with human GLP-1. Available as Byetta (twice daily) and Bydureon (once weekly extended release).
mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonism stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon, and slowing gastric emptying.
usage: Subcutaneous injection 60 minutes before morning and evening meals (Byetta). Bydureon once-weekly formulation.

name: Pinealon
tagline: Pineal peptide bioregulator with neuroprotective and anti-ageing properties
description: Pinealon is a synthetic tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) derived from the bovine pineal gland, part of the Khavinson peptide bioregulator series. Research in Russia shows neuroprotective effects, improved cognitive function, and circadian rhythm regulation.
mechanism: Penetrates the blood-brain barrier; epigenetically modulates gene expression related to melatonin synthesis, antioxidant defence (SOD, catalase), and neuronal survival.
usage: Oral capsule or sublingual. Course-based: 10–14 day courses, 2–4× per year.

name: Cortagen
tagline: Lung and bronchial tissue bioregulator peptide
description: Cortagen is a tetrapeptide bioregulator (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) derived from bovine cerebral cortex. Part of Khavinson's peptide bioregulator series; studied for neuroprotective and pulmonary tissue restoration effects.
mechanism: Short peptides act epigenetically to modulate transcription factor binding and gene expression in target tissues, restoring protein synthesis in ageing cells.
usage: Subcutaneous injection or oral capsule. Course-based: 10-day courses twice yearly.

name: Cerebrolysin
tagline: Multi-target neuroprotective peptide mixture approved in Europe & Asia
description: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture containing neurotrophic factors and neuropeptides. Approved in several European and Asian countries for stroke, traumatic brain injury, and Alzheimer's disease. Studies show BDNF-like effects.
mechanism: Contains biologically active peptide fragments mimicking NGF and BDNF activity, promoting neuronal survival, reducing neuroinflammation, and inhibiting apoptotic pathways in neurons.
usage: Intravenous infusion (clinical setting) or intramuscular injection. Typically 5–30 mL IV in courses of 10–21 days.
typicalDoseRange: 5 – 30 mL IV per day for 10–21 day courses

name: Adamax (NA-1 / Tat-NR2B9c)
tagline: Neuroprotective peptide targeting NMDA excitotoxicity in stroke
description: Nerinetide (NA-1) is a 9-amino acid peptide fused to the HIV TAT protein for CNS penetration. It uncouples NMDA receptors from downstream excitotoxic death pathways, showing neuroprotection in animal models and mixed results in human stroke trials.
mechanism: Blocks the interaction of NR2B (GluN2B) C-terminal domain with PSD-95 scaffolding protein, preventing NMDA receptor-mediated excitotoxic calcium influx during ischemia.
usage: IV administration only (clinical research). Not available for self-administration.

name: Kisspeptin
tagline: Hypothalamic peptide that drives GnRH pulsatility and fertility
description: Kisspeptin (KISS1 gene product) is the key upstream regulator of GnRH pulsatility. It is essential for puberty onset and reproductive function. Research use includes fertility stimulation, hypogonadism, and testosterone optimisation.
mechanism: Binds GPR54 (KISS1R) on GnRH neurons in the hypothalamus, triggering GnRH pulse secretion, downstream LH/FSH release, and gonadal steroid production.
usage: Subcutaneous injection pulsed to mimic endogenous kisspeptin rhythmicity. Research protocols use 1–10 nmol/kg doses.

name: GDF-11 (Growth Differentiation Factor 11)
tagline: TGF-β family member with potential rejuvenating effects
description: GDF-11 is a TGF-β superfamily member that received significant interest following parabiosis studies suggesting it could reverse age-related cardiac hypertrophy. Subsequent research has been mixed, but it remains an active area of longevity investigation.
mechanism: Activates ALK4/ALK5 receptors and SMAD2/3 signalling pathways; may inhibit age-related cardiac hypertrophy via reducing β-MHC expression and promoting cardiomyocyte homeostasis.
usage: Research-grade subcutaneous injection. No established human dosing protocol; studies use microgram-level doses.

name: CKB (Creatine Kinase Brain-type) / Creatine
tagline: Classic ergogenic for strength, power, and cognitive support
description: Creatine monohydrate is the most evidence-backed sports supplement, increasing phosphocreatine stores for rapid ATP regeneration. Emerging research also supports cognitive benefits, particularly in sleep-deprived or vegetarian individuals.
mechanism: Replenishes phosphocreatine via creatine kinase, enabling rapid ATP resynthesis during high-intensity exercise. May also have neuroprotective effects via brain energy metabolism support.
usage: Oral powder or capsule. 3–5 g/day maintenance; 20 g/day loading phase (optional, 5–7 days).

name: AC-262 (Acetamidoxolutamide)
tagline: Selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) with tissue-selective anabolism
description: AC-262536 is a non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) demonstrating ~66% of testosterone's anabolic activity in muscle with only ~27% of androgenic activity in the prostate in animal studies. Under research; not approved for human use.
mechanism: Binds androgen receptor selectively, acting as a partial agonist in muscle/bone and partial antagonist/weak agonist in prostate, providing tissue-selective anabolic signalling.
usage: Oral capsule. Research protocols use 10–30 mg/day in 8–12 week cycles with PCT (post-cycle therapy) recommended.

name: NMN / NR (NAD+ Precursors)
tagline: Boosts cellular NAD+ for sirtuin activation and longevity pathways
description: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) are NAD+ precursors that efficiently raise intracellular NAD+ levels. NAD+ declines with age; replenishing it activates sirtuins (SIRT1–7), PARPs, and CD38, supporting mitochondrial function and DNA repair.
mechanism: Converted to NAD+ via the salvage pathway; activates SIRT1/SIRT3 (mitochondrial biogenesis, fat oxidation), SIRT6 (DNA repair), and PARP1 (genomic stability). Also raises NADH for electron transport chain function.
usage: Oral capsule or sublingual NMN. 250–500 mg/day NMN or NR is typical; some longevity protocols use up to 1 g/day.

name: FGL (NCAM-derived Peptide)
tagline: NCAM-mimetic peptide enhancing synaptic plasticity and memory
description: FGL is a synthetic peptide derived from the second fibronectin type III module of neural cell adhesion molecule (NCAM). It mimics homophilic NCAM binding and activates intracellular FGF receptor signalling, enhancing LTP and spatial memory.
mechanism: Activates FGF receptor and downstream Akt/PI3K pathway via NCAM mimicry; enhances long-term potentiation (LTP) magnitude and promotes dendritic spine density in the hippocampus.
usage: Subcutaneous injection in research protocols. 2–8 mg/kg doses in animal studies; human research protocols ongoing.

name: Retatrutide
tagline: Triple GLP-1/GIP/Glucagon agonist — next-generation weight loss
description: Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational triple-agonist targeting GLP-1R, GIPR, and glucagon receptor (GCGR) simultaneously. Phase 2 trial data showed up to 24% body weight reduction over 48 weeks, surpassing all existing approved agents. It is currently in Phase 3 trials.
mechanism: Activates GLP-1R (appetite suppression, insulin secretion), GIPR (additive metabolic effect), and GCGR (increased energy expenditure and hepatic fat oxidation), producing complementary and synergistic weight-loss effects.
usage: Subcutaneous injection once weekly. Phase 2 dose escalation up to 12 mg. Not yet approved; available only in clinical trials.

name: 5-Amino-1MQ
tagline: NNMT inhibitor that reverses metabolic dysfunction and promotes fat loss
description: 5-Amino-1-methylquinolinium (5-Amino-1MQ) is a small-molecule inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme overexpressed in obese adipose tissue. By inhibiting NNMT, it raises NAD+ and SAM levels, activates SIRT1 pathways, reduces fat cell size, and improves insulin sensitivity. Animal studies show significant fat mass reduction without caloric restriction.
mechanism: Inhibits NNMT enzyme, preventing it from consuming S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) and 1-methylnicotinamide. This raises intracellular NAD+, activates sirtuins, upregulates mitochondrial biogenesis, and reduces lipogenesis in white adipose tissue.
usage: Oral capsule. Research protocols use 75–150 mg doses 1–2× daily. Often cycled 8–12 weeks. No approved human clinical trials yet; used in research community.
